newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Swedes arrive in S.Africa to probe Palme murder.
newsitem.headline: Swedes arrive in S.Africa to probe Palme murder.

text.p: Swedish investigators arrived in South Africa on Thursday to probe allegations that the unsolved assassination of Prime Minister Olof Palme was carried out by apartheid agents.
Palme, shot in a Stockholm street in 1986, was a staunch anti-apartheid activist and a fierce campaigner for sanctions against South Africa.
Swedish chief prosecutor Jan Danielsson, who arrived with the detective heading of the probe into the murder, Hans Oluebro, told a news conference:
"We are very pleased to be here and we have been offered all the help we have asked for. We will stay as long as is necessary."
A possible South African connection to the killing came to light last month when former apartheid secret agents named three different people as having been involved.
All three -- South African spy Craig Williamson, former Rhodesian special forces soldier Ant White and a Swede now living in northern Cyprus -- denied any link to the murder.
Williamson has since been arrested in Angola on unspecified charges.

Danielsson said they might interview some of the agents involved but they would first meet the attorney general of Gauteng province, Jan D'Oliviera, who is probing dirty tricks during the apartheid era.
"We will first have the meeting with the attorney general and then see who we should talk to," he said.
South African Justice Minister Dullah Omar told the news briefing he was not certain if South Africans were involved in the Palme murder but the matter needed to be investigated.
He said the Swedes would given all the assistance they required, including forcing anyone who did not want to talk to appear in court.

"There are formal procedures which can be followed to compel persons to testify," he said. "In our own view anything is possible, especially in the last decade of apartheid rule, and everything needs to be investigated."
